🙆 The art of sincere listening and nodding.
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 2: Pragmatic Communication and Implicit Social Codes 📌 Field:🗣️ Pragmatic communication
🎖️ Today’s Badge: Big Ears Listening Ambassador

👂 Showing I Am Listening: Attention and Body Language

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Special education students often turn their backs to others and fidget with their hands while listening to them, making it seem as if they are not listening at all. We teach them the "Three Treasures of Listening to Body Language": lean slightly forward, look at the other person's forehead, and nod gently after understanding each sentence.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🗿 A wooden figure and a nodding sunflower!

Today Jia excitedly shared with He the interesting story of seeing five little ducks in the park yesterday: "He, look, the mother duck is swimming in the water with the ducklings, and the last duckling almost slipped. It's so cute!""Although He didn't speak, her body was facing Jia, her eyes staring at the eraser in her hand, motionless like a cold wooden statue. As Jia talked, her voice became smaller and smaller, and finally she lowered her head in frustration: "He, you weren't listening to me at all, were you?" I feel so bored..." He hurriedly raised his head: "Yes! I'm listening! You said five little ducks! ” He smiled and said, “He’s ears are listening, but his body is asleep! When others are talking, our body should be like a sunflower, turning towards the sun and facing the speaker. Every time we understand a sentence, we should nod slightly and say "Yeah! Really!", so that the other person can see your sincerity! "He immediately turned around and looked at Jia and nodded: "Jia, please continue, did the little duck catch up with his mother later? ”Jia’s eyes suddenly lit up!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:If a classmate keeps looking down at something and ignoring you while you're talking, would you want to continue talking to them? How can you use actions to let the other person know you're listening attentively?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:Partners share wonderful life experiences, and the four little heroes practice using body language to demonstrate sincere listening!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Put down the building blocks in your hand, turn your body towards Jia who is speaking, focus your eyes on Jia's brow, and nod gently.
"Jia, I'm listening!" Five little ducks are swimming in the water, what next? ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to overcome the eye avoidance habit and convey social goodwill with active orientation.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Place both hands on your thighs without playing with the pen, lean your body slightly forward, and nod earnestly in agreement.
"Hmm!" I listened carefully! Did the little duck get home safely in the end? ”
💡 Tips:Help Jun to converge its restless limbs into a stable listening structure.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Face Jia like a little sunflower, with a smile on your face, and listen attentively to every word your partner says.
"Now I have learned to be a sunflower!"Seeing you nodding, I know you are so happy today!”
💡 Tips:Help He externalize inner focus into warm limbs that make peers feel respected.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Seeing your peers looking at you so attentively and nodding makes you more vivid and confident in your sharing.
"You are all looking at me and listening to me. I feel so happy!" Finally, the mother duck rescued the duckling ashore! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to experience the positive motivational feedback of being sincerely listened to by peers.

1
Turn your chair or shoulder so that your body is facing the student who is speaking.
2
Look at the other person's forehead or the bridge of their nose to show focus.
3
Each time I understood a passage, I nodded slightly downwards and smiled.
🎯 IEP Quantitative Goals & Putt Collaboration & Family Life Behavioral classification tripartite connection
🎯 IEP observable quantitative goals:When listening to a peer's individual speech for 1 minute, be able to maintain the body facing the other person and have a listening response of nodding or directional gaze, without turning away or ineffective distraction, and the achievement rate is above 85%.
🏫 Post-it notes on integration tips for regular class instructors:
The "Best Audience Award" can be set up when the general class reports in groups, specifically to praise the group members who can use body language to affirm the speaker.
🏠 Home Practice Check-In:
After returning home from school, show your parents how to🙆 Listen sincerely and nod", and give warm high-fives to your family!

🔹 Students with autism spectrum disorder (ASD)
Use the "body turn + eyebrow gaze + three micro nods" step card to internalize implicit listening into explicit body movements.
🔹 Students with Learning Disabilities (LD)
Matching feedback formula: "Wow! Then what? Really! ”Enrich the interactive language of listening.
🔹 Students with Emotional Disorders (EBD)
Practice refraining from interruptions and interruptions, and maintain a listening position with your hands flat on your knees for 1 minute.

❓ When Instructions Are Confusing: Ask for the Next Step Again

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Faced with multiple instructions from the teacher, such as "Take out the blue notebook, turn to page 25, write the third question, and hand it in to the group leader," children with learning disabilities and autism often freeze up due to insufficient working memory. The teachers encourage students to raise their hands and ask to repeat the specified steps.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🌪️ A long strip of paper flies away and a brave little hand is raised!

During the nature class, I explained four things in one breath: "Please put away your pencil case first, take out the yellow observation record book, turn to page 18 and draw today's bean sprouts, and give it to the group leader to stamp after you finish!" "He sat in his seat, a big tornado was blowing through his head. He only remembered the first sentence to put away the pencil box, and everything after that became a mess! Seeing the classmates around him taking out their notebooks and starting to draw, He was so anxious that his eyes were red, and he sat at a loss in his seat in a daze. He wanted to peek at the classmates next to him but didn't dare. He came over and touched He's head gently: "He, it's normal not to understand or remember. Your brain needs some time to download!"Don't be in a daze and pretend to understand, raise your little hand and tell: "Please tell me again what to do in the second step?" He wiped away his tears and mustered up the courage to raise his right hand: "Report, I can't hear the third step clearly. Who should I give it to after finishing the painting?"” He smiled and said, “That’s a great question! Give it to the team leader to get it stamped!”He immediately took out his notebook and started working happily!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When you are told many things that you cannot understand or remember, is it useful to sit in a daze in your seat? How do I ask so that I can understand the steps?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:When a multi-step task was explained in class and the student didn't understand, the four little heroes practiced raising their hands to confirm the steps without panicking!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Remember only the first two steps, take out your own sticky notes on the desk, raise your hand and ask the teacher to confirm the third step.
"Teacher, I have turned to page 18. Who should I hand over to the third step?"”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to proactively use spoken language to check specific implementation details to reduce anxiety.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Quickly put away the pencil case, and enthusiastically turn around to quietly remind He in the same group of the page number.
"Look, He, turn to this page to draw bean sprouts!" Let me open the book for you! ”
💡 Tips:Guide students to exert their enthusiasm for helping others and promote cooperative learning among peers.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Bravely raise your right hand, with a firm look in your eyes, and clearly ask the teacher to repeat the instructions.
"Teacher, there are too many steps for me to remember. Could you please tell me the last step again?"”
💡 Tips:Help He overcome low self-esteem and shrinkage, and establish a sense of learning rights to actively ask for help.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Mark the three large numbers 1, 2, and 3 with a pattern on the blackboard with chalk to help the whole class visually memorize them.
"I wrote the steps on the blackboard!" The first step is to collect the pencil case, the second step is to draw beans, and the third step is to stamp it! ”
💡 Tips:Guidingjia benefits all students through the structured construction of the environment.

✏️ Writing Frustration: Put Down the Pencil and Take a Break

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Children with learning disabilities and motor coordination difficulties often tear their notebooks due to insufficient hand muscle strength, resulting in inconsistent handwriting, writing outside the lines, and excessive force when scratching. Guiding children to "put down the pen, rub their hands, and use patching stickers to repair the damage" helps build resilience.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
💣 Angry torn paper and magical transparent repair sticker!

During the vocabulary practice class, He held a thick triangular pencil tightly in his hand. Because my hand coordination is relatively weak, the thirteen horizontal lines on the right side of the word "listen" cannot fit into the square grid no matter how I write it, and it accidentally flies out of the grid! He picked up the eraser and rubbed hard, and the result was "Hiss——!""With a sound, a big black hole was wiped out of the thin calligraphy pad! Looking at the broken notebook, He collapsed. Tears fell like broken pearls. He grabbed the entire calligraphy notebook and tried to tear it into pieces! With bright eyes and quick hands, he gently held He's wrist: "He, take a deep breath!" Your hands are too hard and too hard! Put down the pencil first and let’s do the “dough finger exercise”! ” He took out a small piece of green clay and let He squeeze it to relax his tense fingers. Then he took out a roll of transparent invisible tape and said, “It doesn’t matter if the paper is torn. We put on a piece of “Repair Velcro” and the hole will be repaired. Let’s write it again! ”He wiped away his tears, touched the flat tape, picked up the pen again, and wrote the words correctly one stroke at a time!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When you can't write well or tear your notebook, will tearing the notebook make your handwriting neater? How can you relax when your hand is sore and you feel frustrated?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:Feeling frustrated and overwhelmed by erasing their pencils while writing, the four little heroes practice putting down their pencils, relieving the pressure on their fingers, and repairing the notebooks!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:If you feel frustrated when writing outside the lines, take a deep breath, place the pen flat on the table, close your eyes, and count to five.
"It doesn't matter if the words exceed the grid, I will erase them and write slowly without losing my temper and dirtying the notebook!"”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to overcome the compulsive fixation on perfect grid lines and accept reasonable stroke errors.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:When you see a fellow student about to tear up their notebook, immediately hand them transparent tape and encourage them with a firm tone.
"Don't tear it up, He!" It’s even more tiring to tear it up and have to rewrite it! Just put some tape on it and it will look like new! ”
💡 Tips:Guide people to experience impulse and turn it into timely positive persuasion from sympathetic peers.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Put down the pencil, squeeze the soft clay in your palms to relax your fingers, and then apply the repair sticker.
"Phew~ My hands are relaxed!"The magic tape was put on, the hole was repaired, and I could write again!”
💡 Tips:Help He experience the sense of control after hand pressure reduction, and overcome frustration.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Gently place the pencil grip on He's pencil and adjust the angle of the pencil tip grip.
"With this soft pencil holder, your hands won't be so sore. Let's work hard together!"”
💡 Tips:Guide and use auxiliary teaching aids to provide partners with substantial support.

1
I noticed my fingers were stiff, and I felt an urge to angrily stab the paper.
2
Immediately put down the pencil, and make five kneading motions in the air with both hands as if kneading dough.
3
Take out some transparent repair tape, cover the hole, take a deep breath, and rewrite it.

🤝 Read aloud a relay help card

📖 Reading Aloud: Asking a Partner for Help

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Children with dyslexia often stumble and get stuck when taking turns reading aloud in class due to difficulties recognizing words, skipping lines, or breaking down characters, which can lead to laughter from peers and cause social trauma. Teaching methods can help resolve this by showing a "relay help card" and having group members read a sentence in turn.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
Dancing black ants and a warm relay baton!

In the Chinese language class, ask the whole class to stand up and read a text aloud according to their seat numbers. When it was He's turn, she stood up with her textbook. In He's eyes, the Chinese characters on the textbook were like little black ants dancing in a crooked arrangement. He read the first three words: "Spring...day..." and then got stuck in front of the four words "breeze", and couldn't spell it out no matter how hard he spelled it. The whole class was quiet for five seconds. A few naughty students in the back row began to chuckle: "Why do you read so slowly?"”He's face instantly turned red like a ripe tomato, his legs were shaking, and tears were about to fall down. At this time, Jia, who was sitting in the front row, saw it and immediately raised the "green relay flag" in his hand, smiled and read aloud: "The breeze is blowing the green willow trees!" ” Immediately praised: “Jia did a great job! He also read very clearly!” With the partner relaying, He took a deep breath and finished the next sentence smoothly, and the whole class burst into warm applause!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When you get stuck reading aloud on stage, what would you do if some classmates laughed? What's a good way to ask a good friend to help you finish?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:During class, students took turns reading the text and encountered difficulties with unfamiliar words. The four little heroes practiced a relay race to resolve the awkward situation!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:While seated, point to each line of the text and follow along, silently encouraging He on stage as he reads.
"Come on He, I look at the words in the textbook and can help you read them at any time!" ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu supports peer learning with visual tracking and focused companionship.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:If you hear someone laughing in the back row, immediately turn around and sternly stop them: "Don't laugh! Everyone is learning to read!"
"Everyone, be quiet!"He practices every day. It’s rude to laugh at others!”
💡 Tips:Guide students to use their sense of justice to stop bullying and maintain the psychological safety of the class.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:When you see Jia raise the relay flag, take a deep breath, straighten your chest, and smoothly continue reciting the next sentence.
"Thank you, Jia, for helping me relay!"Now I take a deep breath and read the next sentence!”
💡 Tips:Help He regain courage from peer relay and overcome reading inferiority complex.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Immediately raise the green relay flag and help read the four words that are stuck in a clear and loud voice.
"The breeze is blowing the willow trees!" He, I'll let you continue. You read it very nicely! ”
💡 Tips:Guiding Jia is keenly aware of the difficulties of peers and exerts team spirit to proactively fill in the gaps and provide support.

Establish a "little angel relay mechanism" for class reading, allowing small flags to be displayed on difficult words for peers to read.
🔹 Students with Emotional Disorders (EBD)
When you hear the laughter of your peers, practice saying to yourself in your mind: "It doesn't matter, the words are dancing, I can just find someone to take over."

⏳Tick-tock clock adagio pranayama
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 3: Classroom Learning Frustrations and Homework Challenges 📌 Field:📝 Classroom learning
🎖️ Today’s Badge: Calm Timing Expert

⏱️ The timer in class is ticking and I am so nervous - Facing time pressure, "take a deep breath according to the rhythm and take a breath for each question"

🎯 Summary of core objectives:The shrinking red block or ticking sound of the countdown timer on the large screen often causes autistic and learning-disabled children to experience extreme anxiety, sweaty palms, and a complete mental blank. Teaching children to shift their visual focus to their breathing circle and learn the rhythm of "taking a breath after finishing a problem" is helpful.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
💣 A red countdown bomb and a leisurely little sea turtle!

Today's math class is conducting a ten-minute five-question quiz. A huge red countdown timer is projected in the middle of the electronic whiteboard. Tick ​​tock, tick tock, tick tock... As the red time disk gets smaller round by round, the hands make a rapid electronic sound. Yu, who was sitting in the second row, looked at the red circle and his heart beat so fast that it felt like it was about to jump out of his throat! The pencil in my hand was so tight that my palms were covered in cold sweat. The addition and subtraction calculations I originally knew turned into knotted balls of wool in my head! Yu was so anxious that he crumpled the test paper into a ball: "It's about to explode!"I can’t finish writing anymore!” Walked to the big screen, pressed the "silent mode" of the timer, and placed a slowly flowing "blue turtle liquid hourglass" on Yu's desk: "Yu, time is not a bomb chasing you, but a good friend who accompanies you." Watching the turtle swimming slowly, after writing a question, take a deep breath, and we move forward at our own speed! "Yu watched the turtle descend slowly, exhaled a long breath, restarted his brain, and successfully completed the problem one stroke at a time!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When you see the clock counting down and you feel panicked, will crumpling up the exam paper buy you time? How can you calm your mind and write slowly?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:The timed quiz is in progress, and the four little heroes are practicing overcoming the pressure of time and maintaining steady breathing to answer the questions!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Look at the blue turtle hourglass on the table, take a deep breath and relax your shoulders, then write down the equations one by one in sequence.
"Time is not a bomb. Turtles swim slowly. I will calculate each question one by one. I can figure it out!"”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to replace the anxious countdown stimulus by stabilizing the visual flow rate.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:After finishing the third question, I felt a little anxious, so I put my hands on the table and took a deep breath. I didn't guess the answer randomly before handing in the paper.
"Huh~ I won't make random guesses!" There are still five minutes left. I have to carefully check and calculate the remaining two questions! ”
💡 Tips:Guide students to overcome the impulsive rush mentality and cultivate patience in checking and calculating.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Use a ruler to read the problem line by line slowly. Although the speed is slow, each step is calculated very thoroughly.
"Although I write slowly, the teacher said that you are a true hero if you write what you know how to write correctly!"”
💡 Tips:Guidance and affirmation of self-learning pace, not affected by the speed of peers submitting papers.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Quietly help the whole class maintain a peaceful examination room, and write down the remaining minutes on the blackboard when appropriate.
"Everyone, relax, there is still plenty of time, take a deep breath, and write slowly!"”
💡 Tips:Guidingjia calms the anxiety of the audience through gentle reminders.

🔹 Students with Emotional Disorders (EBD)

🍫 Segment the chocolate into sections
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 3: Classroom Learning Frustrations and Homework Challenges 📌 Field:📝 Classroom learning

📐 Long Word Problems: Breaking Information into Small Parts

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Faced with math literacy word problems that often consist of four or five lines of text, children with reading difficulties and autism often fail to grasp the key words and give up, overwhelmed by the dense text. Teaching them to use a two-color highlighter to solve the problem like "cutting three chocolates" involves breaking down the condition, the number, and the question.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🍫 A giant chocolate block with three magical little cutters!

The last question in the math homework book, the Big Devil question, is four lines long: "There are three classes in the fourth grade of OO Elementary School, each class has twenty-five students. Each excursion ticket for off-campus teaching is one hundred yuan. How much does all the students need to pay in total?" ” As soon as He saw the four rows of densely packed black characters, his scalp felt numb. His eyes skipped lines as he looked at them. He had no idea whether to add or multiply. He held his hair with his hands and sighed: "It's too long!" I can’t even understand why math problems need to be written into storybooks! ” Smiling, he took out a thick chocolate brick and handed Xiaowa a pink and yellow highlighter: “Xiaowa, if you swallow the big chocolate in one bite, you will choke. Let’s cut it into three pieces with a knife! The first cut: find out "who is doing what"; the second cut: circle the "numbers and units"; the third cut: draw "what is the question asking at the end" in yellow! "He followed the instructions and made three cuts. The long question that looked like a monster immediately turned into a refreshing three-step calculation. He shouted excitedly: "It turns out that cutting is so easy! I'll forget it! ”

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When you see a long and difficult question, what happens if you try to guess the answer without even looking at it? Why does using a highlighter to cut through the question make it clearer to the brain?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:Faced with a complex and lengthy math word problem, the four little heroes practice using highlighters to break down the core information into segments!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Use the transparent green reading ruler to cover the irrelevant text below and focus on analyzing the conditional information in the first line.
"Looking slowly, row by row, the first piece of chocolate is from three classes, with twenty-five people in each class!"”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to reduce global information overload interference through visual focusing tools.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Use a pencil to circle the three key numbers 3, 25, and 100 quickly and write out the multiplication equation.
"Circle the numbers so they won't get messed up!" 25 times 3 equals 75, multiply that by 100 and you’re done! ”
💡 Tips:Guide the team to combine agile thinking with step marking to improve computing efficiency.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Use the yellow highlighter to draw the last sentence, and show a bright and confident smile.
"The question asks how much the total ticket cost!" Cut into three pieces of chocolate, and the long questions are no longer scary at all! ”
💡 Tips:Help He experience the reading comprehension breakthrough brought by visual deconstruction.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Draw a diagram of the three tour buses on the whiteboard to help the whole group visually verify the results.
"Draw three pictures of tourist buses, and everyone can see at a glance whether the calculations are correct!”
💡 Tips:Guidance and graphical representation are combined to strengthen the logical thinking structure.

🪐 Unique Planetary Pride
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 3: Classroom Learning Frustrations and Homework Challenges 📌 Field:📝 Classroom learning
🎖️ Today’s badge: Creative and confident little painter

🎨 Art Is Unique: Letting Go of Perfection

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Children with autism are often bound by a strong sense of perfectionism and fixation on symmetry. If they paint outside the black lines in their watercolor paintings or their clay sculptures are slightly different from the teacher's model, they may break down in tears, crushing and stomping on their artwork. It is important to guide children to accept that "difference is precisely what makes art unique."

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🌌 A crooked flying saucer and a colorful rainbow star!

The theme of today's art class is to use light clay to build a "magical space station".A neat, symmetrical and neat silver-white rocket model was displayed on the podium. Yu kneaded it, but because the clay was too soft, the tip of the rocket was slightly tilted three centimeters to the left, and it could not be straightened no matter how hard he kneaded it. Yu looked at the crooked rocket, his face turned red, his fists were shaking, he grabbed the rocket and smashed it to the ground, saying, "It's broken!"It looks nothing like it! I'm a big fool!” Wen Wen stretched out her hands to catch Yu’s clay: “Yu, wait! Please look at the clouds outside the window. Are any of them exactly the same? How boring would the universe be if everyone's spaceships looked the same? The tip of your rocket curves to the left, how like a magical cruiser that is quickly dodging an asteroid!"Yu was stunned. He looked at the curved rocket in his hand and suddenly felt so handsome. Yu added two more little stars next to it and smiled happily: "This is my exclusive "Interstellar Scimitar"! ”

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When your drawing or art piece is different from the template, will smashing or stepping on it make you feel better? Why is something different the most special treasure?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:The clay sculpture was accidentally sculpted crookedly. The four little heroes practiced breaking free from the constraints of perfectionism and appreciating unique creativity!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Looking at the crooked rocket, put down your hand that you want to smash, take a deep breath, tilt your head and add yellow clay to turn it into a thruster.
"It's not broken because it's crooked. My rocket is the most flexible interstellar cruiser in the universe!"”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to break the symmetry fixation and reconstruct the unexpected results into unique creative highlights.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:If you accidentally paint outside the black line with watercolor, don't tear off the paper. Instead, use blue to paint a wave pattern.
"It doesn't matter if I paint the outside of the grid, I'll paint it into a big wave and turn it into a super waterfall!"”
💡 Tips:Guidance to transform small setbacks into flexible artistic sense of humor.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Gently sculpt a round little snowman with your hands and happily show your creation to everyone.
"Although my snowman's belly is one big and one small, he is smiling and I think he is so cute!"”
💡 Tips:Help He experience the beautiful feeling of self-acceptance and build positive self-esteem.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Arrange the four different spaceships together in front of the podium to form a space fleet.
"It's fun if all four ships are different!" Together, we are the strongest space fleet in OO Elementary School! ”
💡 Tips:Guide and praise the beauty of heterogeneity and condense the collective sense of honor of diverse integration.

📁 Five-Color Storage Magic
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 3: Classroom Learning Frustrations and Homework Challenges 📌 Field:📝 Classroom learning

🎒 An Organized School Bag: Color Folders and a Daily Check

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Children with ADHD and learning disabilities often have weak executive functions, resulting in their schoolbags being stuffed with crumpled notices, moldy breadcrumbs, and scattered colored pens. They experience anxiety when they can't find their homework during class and are punished. We teach them the "five-color folder sorting method" and a three-minute "detoxification and emptying check" before school ends.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🕳️ A giant black hole backpack and a colorful rainbow folder!

When I collected the Mandarin homework books for early self-study, the whole class had handed them in, and only Jia was still shaking things up in his big school bag! I saw that Jia's schoolbag was stuffed like a big black hole about to explode. Inside, there were last week's notices wrinkled into pickles, broken crayon ends, leftover biscuit bags, and three textbooks with their corners turned upside down. Jia was so anxious that he was sweating profusely and almost going crazy: "Weird!" I clearly wrote something yesterday, but why is it missing? So annoying!” Jia was so angry that he dumped all the sundries in his schoolbag on the corridor floor. He came over and took out five transparent folders of different colors: "Jia, your schoolbag is not a trash can, it is your study toolbox!" Let’s do the “Five Color Detoxification Method”: blue for Mandarin, red for math, yellow for contact books, and green for notifications! ’ Under the guidance of Zai, Xiaojiu threw the sundries into the trash can. The five subjects were neatly arranged in categories. The missing vocabulary book suddenly jumped out of the blue folder! Jia hugged her neat schoolbag and smiled proudly!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:How anxious do you feel when you can't find your homework book during class? What are the benefits of tidying up your schoolbag after school each day for yourself tomorrow?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:It's time to hand in homework during morning self-study. The four little heroes practice using color-coded folders to quickly find their notebooks!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Following the order of blue Mandarin and red Math labels, neatly pull out the vocabulary book from your schoolbag and hand it to the group leader.
"The blue label is for Mandarin homework. I found it right away. The schoolbag is neat and comfortable!"”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to give full play to the strengths of classification and establish a structured school bag order.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Pick up the scraps of paper from your schoolbag and put them in the trash can. Then, neatly arrange the five-colored folders and put them back in your schoolbag.
"Phew~ My big black hole schoolbag has been detoxified!"Now it only takes three seconds to find something!”
💡 Tips:Guide the establishment of executive functions and the organization of personal life items management.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Look at the backpack check card, check the pencil case and communication book one by one, zip up the bag and smile.
"Tick the cards and bring all the homework. You don't have to worry about being missed when you go home today!" ”
💡 Tips:Help He use checklists to overcome forgetfulness anxiety and enhance a sense of autonomy.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Show the neatly organized inner lining of your backpack in front of the podium and encourage everyone to keep it clean.
"It only takes three minutes to pack your schoolbag every day, and you won't be in a hurry to find it in class tomorrow!" ”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to demonstrate good living routines and become a model of cleanliness in the class.

🤝 No complaints when the team drops a baton
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 3: Classroom Learning Frustrations and Homework Challenges 📌 Field:📝 Classroom learning
🎖️ Today’s Badge: Best Teammate

🏃 A Dropped Relay Baton: Supporting a Teammate

🎯 Summary of core objectives:In relay races or team competitions, if a teammate slips the baton or runs the wrong lane, causing the entire group to fall behind, emotionally challenged children are prone to verbally abusing them, shouting things like, "It's all your fault! You're terrible!" This can lead to serious peer bullying. The correct approach is to "immediately go up to them, pat them on the back, and say, 'It's okay, let's catch up together.'"

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🥉 The golden baton rolled off the red track!

On the eve of the school sports meet, during PE class, a tense and exciting fourth-grade relay simulation was underway. Jun ran the fourth leg, sprinting like a whirlwind and successfully catching up to second place! At the baton exchange area, Jun shouted, "Pass the baton!" However, He, who was supposed to receive the fifth leg, was so nervous with sweaty palms that her outstretched hand slipped, and the golden baton slammed onto the red PU track with a loud "thud!" rolling all the way into the grass! The teams behind seized the opportunity to overtake, and the lead instantly turned into last place. Jun's eyes blazed with anger, and she clenched her fists, about to rush towards He and yell, "What are you doing! You're so stupid! You're the one who made us lose!" Seeing this, Jia immediately rushed over, picked up the baton, and shoved it back into He's hand, shouting, "He, don't stop! Keep going! Jun, yelling now will only slow things down, let's all cheer her on from the sidelines!" Jun paused for a moment, watching He grit his teeth and sprint forward. He swallowed the curse words he was about to utter, put his hands to his mouth and shouted, "Go He! Go for it!" The whole class cheered along, and He sprinted like he had a turbocharger, finally catching up with one person just before the finish line!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When a teammate makes a mistake during a competition, will yelling at them on the spot bring back the ranking? Why is saying "It's okay, we'll catch up together" the coolest way to be a teammate?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:During a relay race, a teammate's nervousness caused them to drop the baton, resulting in them falling behind. The four little heroes practiced restraining their blaming and demonstrating team tolerance and drive!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Stand in front of the finish line and wave the cheering flag vigorously, cheering loudly for He who is sprinting after dropping the baton.
"He rushes!" Looking at the finish line ahead, everyone who finishes the race is a hero! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to maintain positive emotional stability and give strength to his peers when he is at a disadvantage in the competition.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Take a deep breath and swallow your accusations, then clap your hands and shout loudly to cheer for He.
"Huh ~ I don't curse!"Come on He! You run very fast, take big strides and rush over!”
💡 Tips:The leader sublimates the aggressive energy into the leadership spirit that unites the team's fighting spirit.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Pick up the baton on the grass, grit your teeth, swing your arms and sprint towards the finish line, without giving up or stopping because of self-blame.
"Everyone didn't scold me and cheered for me. I must run every meter with all my strength!"”
💡 Tips:Help He gain motivation to resist setbacks from the tolerance of peers and persevere to the end.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Quickly guide the baton exchange route and remind everyone not to stand on the track and block the runners.
"Everyone, cheer on both sides of the runway, leave the road to He, we are the number one who will never give up!"”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to maintain order on the field and implement safety and team organization.

📏 Accidentally damaged the Calm Ruler
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 4: Peer Friction and Conflict Resolution Advanced 📌 Field:🤝 Peer conflict

😡 Accident or Intent? Responding Calmly to Broken Things

🎯 Summary of core objectives:When a child with autism or emotional disorders accidentally steps on or breaks their beloved stationery, they often instinctively assume "it was intentional" and retaliate with a punch. Guiding children to "first observe their facial expressions, clarify the accident, and seek compensation and an apology from the teacher" can help prevent the violence from escalating.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
💔 A transparent dinosaur ruler broken in two and a sincere apology letter!

Today's math class had to draw straight lines. Yu took out the limited edition "Luminous Tyrannosaurus Transparent Ruler" that his father had just bought for him, and he felt very proud. At the end of class, Xiaojiu hurriedly ran out of his seat to drink water. He stumbled and accidentally brushed the ruler on the corner of Yu's desk with his elbow, "Pah!"’ with a sound, the precious Tyrannosaurus Ruler fell to the ground and was stepped on by Jia and was broken into two halves! Looking at the broken ruler on the ground, Yu's blood pressure soared, his eyes turned red, and he roared like a beast. He grabbed Xiaojiu by the collar and raised his iron fist: "You deliberately stepped on my Tyrannosaurus Ruler!" I'm going to beat you to death! "Xiaojiu turned pale with fright, crouched his hands in front of his chest and shouted: "I didn't mean it! I really didn't see it! sorry! "Immediately walked forward quickly to separate the two people: "Yu, stop! Take a deep breath! Do you think Jia is stepping on it deliberately with a smile on his face, or is he trembling with fear? You can pay compensation if the item is broken, but hitting someone will completely break your friend's heart!”Yu looked at the frightened Jia and slowly lowered his fist. Xiaojiu immediately ran back to his seat and took out a brand new iron ruler and handed it to Yu: "I'm sorry, Yu. I told my mother after school that I will definitely buy an identical one and give it back to you!""Yu took the iron ruler, and the anger in his heart was finally extinguished.

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When someone breaks your favorite toy or stationery, will punching them fix it? Distinguish between "accidental" and "intentional" damage, and why does it protect friendship?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:A classmate accidentally steps on and breaks a student's beloved stationery. The four little heroes practice restraining their punches, recognizing the accident, and rationally resolving the situation!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Take a deep breath while looking at the broken ruler, release your grip on your classmate's collar, and proactively report to the teacher.
"Huh~ My heart hurts, but I know you were careless. Let's ask the teacher to help discuss compensation!" ”
💡 Tips:Guangyu can still follow rational procedures to protect his rights when his extremely cherished items are damaged.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Lower your hands to show sincerity, do not shirk responsibility or run away, and bow on the spot to admit your mistake.
"I'm sorry Yu!" I ran too fast and bumped into one. I promise to ask my mother to buy a brand new one for you after school!”
💡 Tips:Guide people to have the courage to bear subsequent liability for compensation when they get into trouble, and not to evade with excuses.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Hold the transparent tape and squat down to carefully help put the ruler that was broken in two back together and put it into the bag.
"Don't cry, Yu. I'll help you fix it with tape first. You can still see the tyrannosaurus pattern clearly!" ”
💡 Tips:Help He soothe the client's frustration and anxiety with gentle restorative actions.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Take out the class life agreement notebook, record the incident fairly, and guide both parties to shake hands and make peace.
"No one wants the accident to happen. Jia sincerely apologizes and promises compensation. Yu forgives. We are still good friends!" ”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to use fair mediation procedures to maintain the rule of law and peace in the class.

🌐 An Open and Friendly Mind
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 4: Peer Friction and Conflict Resolution Advanced 📌 Field:🤝 Peer conflict
🎖️ Today’s badge: Good friends with broad hearts

👥 Sharing Friends: Making Room for Other Friendships

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Children with autism often have a strong sense of possessiveness and ownership in their friendships. If a close friend talks to other classmates or joins a group, they may feel betrayed, become angry, and break off the friendship or threaten to do so. We should teach them that "everyone can have many friends, and sharing with friends is more fun."

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🎈 A giant balloon with two ropes and a three-person jump rope team!

In the special education classroom, He always felt that Jia was his "most exclusive good friend".Every day after class they sit together in the shade of a tree and draw. After class today, Jia ran excitedly with a skipping rope to play "three-person jump rope" with two girls from the regular class. Everyone laughed so happily in the corridor. He, who was sitting by the window, watched this scene, feeling sore and painful as if a jar of jealousy had been overturned. He was so angry that he bit the pencil in his mouth, his eyes were red, and he secretly swore in his heart: "Jia betrayed me!"She goes to play with others, and I don’t want to deal with Jia anymore!"Going to He, he smiled and took out a bunch of colorful balloons: "He, do you think the balloons look better when held in one hand, or do you think they look better when they are floating in the sky for everyone to see? Friends are not dolls to be locked away in our own closets. Just because Jia goes to jump rope, it doesn't mean that she doesn't like you anymore; if you walk over and ask loudly: "Can I help you shake the rope?" Wouldn't you become good friends among the four of you?"He wiped away his tears and walked out and said loudly: "Jia, let me help you shake the rope! ”The four people held hands and jumped in the sunshine, laughing louder than before!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When your favorite friend goes to play with someone else, can getting angry and severing ties bring them back? Why is it that accepting that a friend has other friends helps the friendship last?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:Seeing their best friend having fun with other classmates, the four little heroes practice letting go of their possessiveness and actively integrating into the group!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Seeing that Jun, whom she usually reads dinosaur books with, was playing dodgeball with others, she went to the library to read books, looking relaxed.
"Jia is very happy to play ball, and I can also enjoy dinosaur time in the library. We are still good friends after school! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to establish healthy social differentiation and ability to handle herself independently.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Seeing He standing to the side watching, the child runs over and waves, inviting him: "He, come play with me!"
"Come on He!" We are short of a super captain who can rock the rope. You are the best and most stable! ”
💡 Tips:The guidance department will pay keen attention to the single peers and actively build bridges for integration.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Put aside your jealousy and anxiety, walk forward confidently, pick up the jump rope handle, and laugh with everyone.
"Let me help you shake the rope!" Seeing everyone jumping so high makes me feel so happy!”
💡 Tips:Help He break the narrow sense of interpersonal exclusivity and experience the joy of group acceptance.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:After jumping rope, the first person to run over and give He a tight hug to thank him for his hard work swinging the rope.
"Thank you, He!" Only if you help us shake the rope can we jump to a new record of thirty times! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to give exclusive emotional guarantee and affirmation to peers in a timely manner.

I sensed a pang of possessive jealousy, a feeling of wanting to get angry and break off the friendship.

🔹 Students with Learning Disabilities (LD)
Use children's songs to establish concepts: "One person plays alone, two people play warm, and everyone has fun!"
🔹 Students with Emotional Disorders (EBD)
Before jealousy breaks out and you want to break off the relationship, take three deep breaths and practice taking the initiative to join in or find other interesting things to do by yourself.

🗣️ Hurtful Nicknames: Speak Firmly and Ask a Teacher for Help

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Special needs students are often teased by their peers behind their backs for their unusual movements or stuttering, being called "freaks," "robots," or "fat boys." The goal is to teach these students to activate their "verbal defense" by giving them a firm look and saying, "That's not my name, please call me by my real name!" and to proactively report such remarks to their teachers.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🦔 Spiky, offensive labels and glittering name badges!

While walking in the corridor, two senior classmates laughed and laughed from behind: "Look, that robot that walks like a penguin is here again!" robot! Beep beep beep!"Xiaojiu, who was walking in front, heard this and knew that they were laughing at his usual way of swinging his arms harder when walking. The three words "robot" pierced Jia's ears like a poisonous sting! Xiaojiu was instantly furious, turned around, grabbed the lid of the trash can next to him, and was about to throw it at the opponent's head! Jia happened to be passing by, and immediately grabbed Jia's arm and shouted: "Jia, stop it!" If you hit someone, you lose. They just want to see you angry! "Jia stood up in front of Jia, looked straight at the two teasing students, and said in a loud and firm voice, "He has a name, his name is Jia from OO Elementary School! It's very rude to call others random nicknames! We will report to the Academic Affairs Office now! "When the two classmates saw Jia being so determined and brave, their faces turned red with fright, lowered their heads and ran away dejectedly. Jia put down the lid of the bucket and took a deep breath: "Thank you, Jia. If I had done something just now, I would have been given a serious demerit!"”

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When someone calls you an unpleasant nickname, if you get angry and hit them on the spot, who will be punished? Fight back with a firm and confident attitude and ask, why is it the smartest thing to do?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:The four little heroes are provoked by malicious and offensive nicknames in the corridor. They practice activating their verbal defense shield, firmly defending themselves, and seeking legitimate means!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:When you hear malicious provocation, stand up straight, look the other person straight in the eye, and speak calmly and firmly.
"Please stop your behavior!"My name is Yu, don't call me any nickname!”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to establish self-dignity with confident, unflinching body and spoken language.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Put down the trash can lid you've grabbed, take a deep breath, and restrain the urge to retaliate with violence.
"Hoo~ I won't fall into your trap!" If you take action, you will only get a demerit. I will report to the instructor now! ”
💡 Tips:Guide people to see clearly the traps behind provocations and choose wise and legal channels for safeguarding their rights.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Stand by Jun's side and hold his hand tightly, offering him unwavering support and companionship.
"Don't be afraid, Jia, we are all here to support you, let's go find the teacher together!"”
💡 Tips:Help He play the role of sympathetic supporter to avoid being left alone by the victimized peers.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Bravely step forward and look the provocateur in the eye, and firmly point out the errors and consequences of their remarks.
"Calling people ugly nicknames is bullying!"Please apologize to Jia immediately, otherwise we will report it to the Academic Affairs Office immediately!”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to develop a sense of justice and use the legal and school rules to fight against bullies.

🤝 Group Decisions: Voting and Respecting Everyone

🎯 Summary of core objectives:When creating posters or discussing topics in groups, autistic children often become fixated on their own ideas, insisting that the entire group listen to their chosen theme, otherwise they will bang on the table, get up, and cry. We should teach them democratic compromise mechanisms such as "majority rule," "best-of-three," and "incorporating different elements."

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🦖 Green Dinosaur vs. 🚀 The decisive battle of Silver Rocket!

During the group activity time in the special education classroom, the four little heroes Yu, He, Jia, and Zhen were asked to work together to draw a large poster of "Our Dream Paradise" on the blackboard. As soon as the discussion topic started, Yu slammed the table loudly: "You must draw "Tyrannosaurus Jurassic Park"! Only dinosaurs are the strongest! All have to draw dinosaurs! ” Jia immediately jumped up and retorted: "No!" Dinosaurs every time! I want to draw "Space Mars Base"! The silver rocket is the most handsome! "The two people refused to give in to each other, and the quarrel got louder and louder. Yu was so angry that he threw the blackboard eraser on the ground, turned around with his arms folded and shouted: "If you don't draw dinosaurs, I will quit, and I will stop drawing them all! "At this time, Jia came over and drew a line in the middle of the blackboard: "Stop! Don't make any noise, everyone! If we have different opinions, we have the ultimate democratic trick - voting and integration! If three people invest in a space base, the minority must obey the majority; but! We can draw a "Tyrannosaurus guard wearing a space helmet" at the gate of the space base. Then wouldn't dinosaurs and rockets be in the same paradise? "Yu was stunned for a moment, imagining the Tyrannosaurus rex wearing a space hat, and couldn't help but burst out laughing: "Okay! A T. rex wearing a space hat sounds really cool! ”The four people immediately picked up the chalk and happily worked together to complete the best space dinosaur base in the school!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:During group discussions, if everyone insists on their own ideas and refuses to compromise, can the task be completed? Why can voting and combining everyone's ideas lead to a win-win situation?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:The group was stuck on the poster theme, so the four little heroes practiced using voting and creative ideas to reach a consensus as a whole!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Let go of your stubborn insistence and accept the compromise of changing your dinosaur into a space tyrannosaurus and integrating it into the rocket base.
"Okay!" It’s not all Jurassic, but the tyrannosaurus in the space hat is really cool, I agree! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to demonstrate cognitive flexibility and compromise mind under the rules negotiation structure.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Stand in front of the blackboard and act as the democratic moderator, proposing a creative solution that integrates the ideas of both sides.
"Arguing cannot solve the problem!" Everyone takes a step back. Dinosaurs wear spacesuits. The opinions of the whole group are taken into account!”
💡 Tips:Guidance turns leadership into team wisdom for coordinating conflicts and resolving deadlocks.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Pick up a piece of chalk and draw a cute star next to the rocket to applaud the team's reconciliation.
"Everyone is no longer angry. It's happiest to paint together!" I painted a shiny helmet for the Tyrannosaurus! ”
💡 Tips:Help He actively engage in cooperative tasks to create a warm and positive team atmosphere.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Take the initiative to step forward and extend your hand to give Yu a high five, acknowledging Yu's magnanimity and cooperative spirit.
"Yu, thank you for your willingness to compromise!" After I finish drawing the space base, I will definitely listen to your ideas for the next theme! ”
💡 Tips:Guidance shows the democratic majority's gratitude to the compromiser and its commitment to future turns.

When your opinion is rejected and you want to quit in anger, take three deep breaths and read the mantra aloud: "The minority obeys the majority, and it will be mine next time!"”

💔 A Dried-Out Marker: Asking Kindly to Make Things Right

🎯 Summary of core objectives:When a kind person lends out colored pens, the cap may not be properly closed when the pens are returned, causing them to dry out and stop writing. Students often become upset and angry, yelling, "You did that on purpose! Pay me back! I'll never lend you a pen again!" Guiding students to use objective facts and gently request a pen loan or to work together to find an alternative solution is helpful.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🍂 A dry, red colored pencil and a box of large, colorful puzzle pieces!

In art class, Jia kindly lent his twenty-four color pens to Xiao Ming in the next group to paint big red flowers. Unexpectedly, when I took it back after class, the most commonly used "big red" pen had not been capped for the entire class. The pen tip had become as dry and hard as a dead branch, and I could no longer draw any color on the paper! Seeing that her beloved pen was broken, Jia's heart felt as if she had been pricked by a needle. She was so angry that she almost shed tears. She really wanted to rush over and smash Xiaoming's pencil case to the ground and yell, "You big bad guy!"Pay me a new pen! ” He walked up to Jia and handed him a glass of warm water to soak the dry tip of the pen: “Jia, it’s normal to be angry, because you feel bad that the pen is broken. But yelling will only make Xiao Ming feel that you are swearing. We can start the "gentle repair dialogue method": point out the facts, express distress, and propose specific compensation methods!"Jia took a deep breath, walked over and said calmly to Xiao Ming: "Xiao Ming, this pen dried up without the cap on. I'm very sad that I can't draw now. Can you please lend me your red pen for this class first, and then buy a single red pen and return it to me next week? "Xiao Ming felt very guilty when he saw the dried pen. He quickly handed his red pen to Jia with both hands: "Jia, I'm sorry! I was too careless. I will definitely ask my mother to buy new ones for you when I get home today! ”A possible quarrel storm turned into a spring breeze in an instant.

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When something you lent to someone gets broken, will yelling at them or even physically smashing their things fix it? Why is it that asking for compensation in a calm and objective tone is more likely to elicit sincere reparations?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:The colored pencils lent to classmates dried out because the caps were not put back on. The four little heroes practiced calmly communicating and expressing their need for repair!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Help by taking out a small measuring cup filled with warm water and soaking the dried pen tip to perform emergency stationery treatment.
"Don't panic, Jia, soak the pen tip in warm water, maybe the ink inside can be saved!" ”
💡 Tips:Guidance Yu uses objective tool operations to focus on problem repair and resolve tensions.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Take out the red spinning crayon from your pencil case and hand it to Jia to use first, thus solving the immediate problem.
"Jia, let me lend you my big red crayon to draw!"Draw slowly, don't rush!”
💡 Tips:Guidance to show the spirit of friendship and mutual help.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Carefully check the cap of each colored pen to make sure that each one is locked with a "click".
"Every pen cap needs to click tightly so the ink doesn't dry out!"”
💡 Tips:Help He establish good living habits of loving and cherishing things carefully.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Control your anger, speak calmly and clearly to the other party, point out the facts, and offer reasonable suggestions for compensation.
"Xiao Ming, the pen was not capped and dried up. I feel very sad. Please lend me your red pen first. Can you buy one and return it to me next week?"”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to use mature non-violent communication to defend his own rights and interests and promote reconciliation.

Provide "stationery first aid life tips" such as soaking pen tips in warm water and dripping glycerin to divert anger from physical repair.

🏃 After a Collision: Check on the Other Person First

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Hyperactive and impulsive children often run quickly down the hallways after school, accidentally knocking down younger students at corners. These children often run away out of fear of punishment or accuse the other child of blocking their way. We should teach them the responsibility of immediately crouching down to help them up and accompanying them to the health center.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🚀 An unstoppable jet plane and a small water bottle on the ground!

As soon as the get out of class bell rang, the fourth-grade student rushed all the way from the classroom door like a fully fueled jet fighter! He spread his hands like wings, moved fast and fast, and shouted: "Whoops!"The plane is landing! ” As soon as I passed the corner of the stairs, a first-grade boy holding a small colorful kettle came out. Jia was too fast and couldn't stop the car, "Bang!""With a sound, the two people collided hard! The little brother was knocked to the ground and sat on the floor. The kettle fell far away. His knees were scratched and bleeding. He cried loudly on the spot! Jia was so frightened that her heart almost jumped out of her chest. Her first reaction was to turn around and run away to the classroom to pretend that nothing was wrong. At this time, someone from behind shouted: "Xiaojiu!" A true hero doesn't run away when he gets into trouble, he stops! "Xiaojiu suddenly stepped on the brakes, turned around and saw his little brother crying with snot and tears on the ground. Xiaojiu gritted his teeth, turned around and ran back to his little brother, squatted down, and gently helped him pick up the kettle: "I'm sorry, little brother! Big brother ran too fast and bumped into you. Where does it hurt? I'll take you to the health center to apply medicine! ”Xiaojiu carefully lifted up his little brother and slowly walked to the infirmary step by step. Although Jia was reminded not to run in the corridor, the nurse aunt praised Jia: "You take care of your juniors responsibly. You are a brave and responsible man!" ”

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When you accidentally knock down a younger student while running, what serious consequences will it cause if you turn and run away? Why is it that "crouching down to check on them and helping them apply medicine" shows you're a responsible older brother?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:While running around a corner, the four little heroes accidentally bumped into a younger student. They practiced overcoming their instinct to run away, crouching down to check on him, and taking responsibility for his care!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:If you witness a collision, immediately step forward and help pick up the water bottle and textbooks that have fallen to the ground.
"Don't cry, little brother, the lid of the kettle is not broken, I will hold it for you!" Jia is helping you! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to exert objective and calm auxiliary support ability at the accident scene.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Overcome your fear of running away, turn around and squat down next to your junior, gently pat your junior's back, and look at him with apology and care in your eyes.
"I'm sorry, little brother, it was the big brother who rushed too fast and bumped into you!" I'll take you to the health center to apply medicine. Don't be afraid if you walk slowly!”
💡 Tips:Guide students to break through the defensive psychology of making mistakes and demonstrate the responsibility of senior students.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Immediately run into the next classroom to inform the teacher and guide the teacher to come and assist in the situation.
"Report to the teacher, a younger brother in the lower grade fell down around the corner, and Jia is accompanying him!"”
💡 Tips:Help He quickly activate the adult support system to ensure medical and treatment safety.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Stand at the corner, make a slow-down gesture with both hands to remind the students running behind you to slow down.
"A classmate fell down at the corner of the corridor!" Please all students behind you please walk slowly and keep to the right! ”
💡 Tips:Guide and maintain safe movement lines around the accident site to avoid secondary collisions.

⚖️ Fair Play: Ask a Neutral Person to Check the Rules

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Special education students exhibit a strong fixation on rules and a strong sense of justice when playing Monopoly, stacking cups, or card games. If they discover that a peer has taken an extra step or an extra card, they immediately assume "he's cheating" and slam their fist on the table to overturn the outcome. They are taught to "pause with their hands forming a 'T' shape with their chest, take out the instruction manual, and check it calmly."

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🎲 The dice rolled a little more than usual, just like the Monopoly instruction manual!

Twenty minutes after class, four people in the special education classroom were playing the exciting "Monopoly World Adventure" board game. When it was Xiao Ming's turn to throw the dice, the dice rolled out five points, but when Xiao Ming's car chess piece reached the fourth square, Xiao Ming slipped his hand and jumped directly to the sixth square to buy the high-speed rail station! Jia, who was sitting opposite, had eyes as sharp as an eagle. He slapped the table on the spot, stood up and yelled: "Cheating!"Got it! You moved one extra square on purpose! Big cheater! This round doesn’t count!"Jia was so angry that he reached out and overturned the entire Monopoly board. Banknotes and houses were scattered all over the floor. Xiao Ming was so frightened that he froze in place. He came over and touched Jia's head gently: "Jia, you have a sense of justice when you find that the number of steps is wrong." But when refereeing has to be personable, flipping the board over will just completely ruin the game. When you think there is something wrong with the rules, our superpower action is - "Make a T with both hands in front of your chest" and shout "Pause! Let's read the instructions and count the steps again", so that everyone will admire your professionalism and impartiality! "Jia looked at the banknotes on the floor and squatted down to help pick them up embarrassedly: "I'm sorry Xiao Ming, I shouldn't have lifted the table. Let's count the dice again, we should be here at five o'clock! ”Everyone sat down again, and the game was filled with laughter again!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When playing a board game and you think someone has made a mistake or cheated, will flipping the whole table solve the problem? Why is it that making a pause gesture and calmly checking the rules is more respected?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:A dispute arose over the number of moves during a board game duel. The four little heroes practiced starting and pausing gestures, calmly checking the rules without flipping the table!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Point carefully to the Monopoly grid squares and objectively and fairly recalculate the points for everyone.
"Don't make any noise, everyone. The dice is five o'clock, one, two, three, four, five. The chess piece should stop here!"”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to exert meticulous and accurate observation skills and provide objective data to resolve disputes.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Help pick up the colored banknotes that have fallen on the ground one by one and arrange them neatly, and take the initiative to soothe the opposing emotions.
"It's okay, it's okay, I just looked at the wrong grid. Just go again. Let's continue playing!" ”
💡 Tips:The leader maintains a friendly and gentle approach to the game and maintains harmony with peers.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Take out the Monopoly instruction manual, point to the second rule, and read it aloud to the whole group.
"The instructions are very clear, just slide your hand and return to the previous square!" ”
💡 Tips:Help He make good use of objective written rules as the basis for fair decisions.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Resist the urge to flip the table, make a large "T" sign with both hands in front of your chest to pause, and speak calmly and firmly.
"Pause than T!" I don't lift the table, I am the impartial judge, let's count again! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to transform a strong sense of justice into a civilized and professional refereeing style.

🎯 Super power move visual chart card ⭐ Fair Verification in Three Steps
1
If you notice a suspected violation or a miscount of steps, immediately make a "T" sign to pause.
2
He said calmly, "Everyone, please pause for a moment. Let's go over the rules with the instruction manual."
3
Everyone should double-count to confirm. If it was indeed a slip of the hand and a mistake, go back to the original position and start over.

After returning home from school, show your parents how to⚖️ Fair Suspension Verification Law" and give a warm high-five to the family!

🔹 Students with Learning Disabilities (LD)
Using step counting tags or big dice, the whole group counts "one, two, three" in unison with each step, which is open and transparent.
🔹 Students with Emotional Disorders (EBD)
Before you want to overturn the table, clasp your hands on your stomach, close your eyes and take a deep breath for the count of five.

👩‍🏫 A Substitute Teacher: Keeping Routines and Being Helpful

🎯 Summary of core objectives:When the original teacher is absent and a substitute teacher enters the classroom, it often causes extreme anxiety and maladjustment among autistic students, or students with emotional disorders take the opportunity to cause trouble and disrupt order. Teaching students to "follow established classroom rules and proactively introduce the class schedule to the substitute teacher" demonstrates good manners.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
👓 New glasses on the podium and a little class tour guide!

In the first Chinese language class this morning, the person who walked into the classroom was not a familiar person, but a Zhang who wore silver-rimmed glasses and spoke in a very soft voice. Zhang wrote his name on the blackboard: "I'm going to study today, and I'll be my substitute for the whole day!"” As soon as he saw the change, Yu's whole body tensed up. He clutched his schoolbag with both hands and refused to let it go. He kept repeating: "No!"no! The timetable is broken!”A few naughty classmates in the back row even started eating candies and chasing each other in the corridor. At this time Jia stood up and shouted: "Stand up and salute!"Good morning!"Jia stepped forward and handed Zhang a "Special Education Class Work and Rest Manual" with both hands: "Hello Zhang, we will read a story and take three deep breaths in the first period of every day. I am Jia, the monitor, and we welcome you!"When Yu saw Jia being so calm, he took a deep breath and slowly put down his schoolbag. Zhang smiled and stamped the whole class: "You are the most sensible and well-behaved class I have ever seen!" ”

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:What will happen when a familiar old tutor takes leave or comes to class and deliberately causes trouble? Why is it a true hero to take the initiative to tell the new class good rules?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:A familiar teacher asks for leave, an unfamiliar substitute teacher enters the classroom, and the four little heroes practice controlling their anxiety and causing a commotion, demonstrating exemplary discipline!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Feeling a little uneasy facing a new teacher? Take out your usual visual timetable for reference, sit down comfortably, and take out your textbook.
"Although the teachers are different, the process of the Chinese class is the same, and I can concentrate on following the class!"”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to overcome overreliance on specific people with constancy in task structure.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Resist the urge to eat snacks in front of the substitute teacher and sit up straight.
"I don't take the opportunity to be naughty!" The teacher is not here, so I have to show discipline to the new teacher! ”
💡 Tips:Guide people to turn their competitive spirit into a sense of self-discipline and honor, and establish internal control traits.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Gently offer a cup of warm water to the substitute teacher with both hands to express the class's warm welcome.
"Teacher Zhang, please drink water. Thank you for coming to teach us today. Thank you for your hard work!" ”
💡 Tips:Help He develop the caring and warm qualities, and actively establish friendly teacher-student interactions.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Stand up and lead the class in saluting, hand over the procedure card and proactively explain the speaking rules to the substitute teacher.
"Stand up and salute!" Hello Teacher Zhang, our class has to raise our hands to be called upon before speaking. We are ready! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to give full play to his positive leadership talents and assist substitute teachers in quickly mastering class routines.

💺 New Seats: Three Ways to Get to Know a Classmate

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Children with autism exhibit a strong fixation on spatial locations. When the class reshuffles seating each month, they often cry and kick their desks, refusing to move because they feel they are "leaving their familiar, cozy spot by the window" or "having a classmate they don't like sitting next to them." We teach children to use three icebreaker phrases to help them adapt to new environments.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🗺️ The wind blowing the school desks and chairs and the new neighbor's colored pencils!

The beginning of every month is the day when the whole class of OO Elementary School changes their seats. The results of the lottery were announced: Yu would move from his safe seat in the corner, where there was a wall to lean on, to the second row in the middle, and the person sitting next to him was Yu, who usually spoke very loudly! As soon as he saw the new seat, Yu's heart felt like a heavy blow. He grabbed the corner of the table and refused to let go. Tears welled up in his eyes and he protested loudly: "I don't want to change!" That's my desk! There are too many middlemen, it’s scary! ” Came over and patted Yu’s shoulder gently: “Yu, moving is like a small adventure. Sitting in the middle, you can see the words on the blackboard more clearly, and Jia is very strong and can help you carry the lunch box at any time! Let’s use three “icebreaker mantras” to get to know your new neighbors!” Yu took a deep breath, moved his schoolbag and sat in the middle. Xiaojiu immediately showed a big smile, took out his newly bought dinosaur sticker and gave it to Yu: "Good morning Yu!" From now on we will be good brothers at the same table! ”Yu looked at the dinosaur stickers on the table, and the stone in his heart finally fell to the ground. It turns out that changing seats can also make good friends!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:If someone keeps crying and making a scene in their old seat when we change seats, can we refuse to change? When you move to a new seat, what's the first thing you should say to your new deskmate to make friends?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:The whole class changed seats and drew new neighbors. The four little heroes practiced overcoming spatial fixation, moving around confidently, and taking the initiative to break the ice!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Although you may not be used to being in the center, take a deep breath, arrange your stationery neatly on the table, and greet your deskmate.
"Good morning Jia, we will sit together in the future, please give me your advice!" ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to break the spatial fixation and take the first step to adapt to the new social circle with active speaking.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Enthusiastically help Yu, who sits at the same table, move a chair, and take out stickers to share, showing friendliness and enthusiasm.
"Yu, welcome to the center!" I have a dinosaur sticker for you. Let’s finish the homework together! ”
💡 Tips:Guide students to accept new classmates with enthusiasm and tolerance, and eliminate the anxiety of special education peers.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Wipe the new table clean and smile and nod to the new classmate next door.
"You can see the green trees outside the window from the new seat!" The view from this location is really nice! ”
💡 Tips:Help He explore the positive advantages of the new environment and cultivate an optimistic and adaptive mentality.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Help direct everyone to move the tables and chairs, and remind them to leave an arm's width of space near the aisle.
"Everyone's tables are arranged neatly, the chairs are put in, and the corridors are kept clear and safe!"”
💡 Tips:Guidance Jia plays an organizational maintenance function when the collective environment changes.
